# Introduction

One of the strengths of computational linguistics is the ability to combine
large text corpora with lexical databases.

In this tutorial we will learn how to:

- Import a corpus
- Tokenize text into words
- Calculate word frequencies
- Examine the  Warriner et al. (2013) norms of **Valence**, **Arousal**, and **Dominance**
- Visualize
---

# What are lexical norms?

Lexical norms are databases in which human participants have rated words
along different psychological dimensions.

One of the most widely used datasets is:

> Warriner, Kuperman & Brysbaert (2013)

Participants rated nearly 14,000 English words on three scales.

| Dimension | Meaning |
|------------|----------|
| **Valence** | How pleasant or unpleasant a word is |
| **Arousal** | How exciting or calming a word is |
| **Dominance** | How much control or power is associated with a word |

Examples:

| Word | Valence | Arousal | Dominance |
|------|---------|----------|------------|
| love | High | Medium | Medium |
| death | Low | High | Low |
| puppy | High | Medium | Low |
| dictator | Low | High | High |

---

# Packages

```{r message=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)
library(ggplot2)


# Set working directory to the current directory
this.dir <- dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path)
setwd(this.dir)
```

---

# Loading the corpora

For this example we'll use a simple text file.

```{r}

war <- read.csv("../data/warriner.csv")
brys <- read.csv("../data/brysbaert.csv")
subtlex <- read.csv("../data/SUBTLEX-US.csv")

head(war)
head(subtlex)
```


The important columns are:

```{r}

names(war)
names(brys)
names(subtlex)

```


- Word
- V.Mean.Sum
- A.Mean.Sum
- D.Mean.Sum



# Preparing the norms

Rename the columns to something easier to use.

```{r}

war <- war %>%
      transmute(
        Word = Word,
        valence = V.Mean.Sum,
        arousal = A.Mean.Sum,
        dominance = D.Mean.Sum,
        valence.sd = V.SD.Sum,
        arousal.sd = A.SD.Sum,
        dominance.sd = D.SD.Sum
      
      )

head(war)

```


# Distribution of valence

```{r}

ggplot(war,
       aes(valence)) +

geom_histogram(bins = 30)

```

Questions:

- Is the corpus generally positive?
- Are there many emotionally neutral words?

---

# Distribution of arousal

```{r}

ggplot(war,
       aes(arousal)) +

geom_histogram(bins = 30)

```

---

# Distribution of dominance

```{r}

ggplot(war,
       aes(dominance)) +

geom_histogram(bins = 30)

```


# take a look at valence and arousal as a 

```{r}
ggplot(war, aes(x = arousal, y = valence)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "Arousal (A.Mean.Sum)",
    y = "Valence (V.Mean.Sum)",
    title = "Valence as a Function of Arousal"
  )
```

## calculate correlation
```{r}
cor(war$arousal, war$valence, use = "complete.obs")
```


# Add word labels
```{r}

head(war)
ggplot(war, aes(x = arousal, y = valence, label = Word)) +
  geom_text(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "Arousal (A.Mean.Sum)",
    y = "Valence (V.Mean.Sum)",
    title = "Valence as a Function of Arousal"
  )
```


# Frequency
```{r}
# subset data just to make it more managable
subtlex <- subtlex[,c("Word","SUBTLWF")]
head(subtlex)
```


# Joining norms together

Merge the datasets by Word
```{r}

total <- war |>  
  left_join(brys,
          by = "Word") |> 
  left_join(subtlex, by="Word")

head(total)

```

Many words will have ratings.

Some will not.

---

# Missing values

How many words have ratings?

```{r}

sum(!is.na(total$Conc.M))

sum(is.na(total$Conc.M))

length(unique(total$Word))

nrow(total)
```

## Drop all words that don't have ratings for both concreteness and affect
```{r}
total <- total |> 
  filter(!is.na(Conc.M))
nrow(total)
```

# Average emotional properties

Now calculate the average emotional profile of the corpus.

```{r}

agr <- total %>%
      summarise(
          Mean_Valence = mean(valence, na.rm = TRUE),
          Mean_Arousal = mean(arousal, na.rm = TRUE),
          Mean_Dominance = mean(dominance, na.rm = TRUE),
          Mean_Conc = mean(Conc.M, na.rm = TRUE)
      )

print(agr)
```

# Which emotional words are most frequent?

```{r}
names(total)
total %>%
  arrange(desc(SUBTLWF)) %>%
  head()

```

```{r}
total %>%
  arrange(desc(SUBTLWF)) %>%
  tail()
```

```{r}

```

```{r}
total %>%

```

# Relationship between Valence and Arousal

```{r}

ggplot(total,
       aes(valence,
           arousal)) +

geom_point(alpha = .3)

```

Questions:

- Are positive words highly arousing?
- Are negative words highly arousing?



# Concreteness

```{r}
ggplot(total,
       aes(valence,
           Conc.M)) +

geom_point(alpha = .3)

```

```{r}
ggplot(total, aes(x = Conc.M, y = valence)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  # theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Concreteness",
    y = "Valence (V.Mean.Sum)",
    title = "Valence as a Function of Concreteness"
  )
```

# Frequency and Valence?

```{r}
ggplot(total, aes(x = SUBTLWF, y = valence, label=Word)) +
  geom_text(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  # theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Frequency",
    y = "Valence",
    title = "Valence as a Function of Frequency"
  )
```


# Frequency and Arousal?

```{r}
ggplot(total, aes(x = SUBTLWF, y = arousal, label=Word)) +
  geom_text(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  # theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Frequency",
    y = "Arousal",
    title = "Arousal as a Function of Frequency"
  )
```
